# Sample traces: draft-papon-lake-pq-edhoc §3

One complete exchange per variant, from the lakers prototype. Generated by
`generate_pq_test_vectors` in `lib/src/lib.rs`; regenerate with

```
cargo test -p lakers --no-default-features \
  --features "lakers-crypto/rustcrypto, test-ead-none, lakers/pq, lakers-shared/pq_buffers" \
  -- --ignored generate_pq_test_vectors
```

## What this is, and what it is not

These are **sample traces**, not reproducible test vectors in the sense of RFC 9529.
ML-DSA signing is randomised (hedged), so `SIGNATURE_2` and `SIGNATURE_3` differ on
every run even with every key and the ephemeral KEM pair held fixed -- and with them
`CIPHERTEXT_2`, `TH_3`, `TH_4`, `PRK_out` and everything exported from it. Only
`message_1`, `H(message_1)`, `TH_2` and `PRK_2e` follow from the inputs.

A verifier can therefore *check* each trace end to end -- every signature verifies,
every hash and KDF step recomputes -- but cannot *regenerate* its bytes. Producing
byte-reproducible vectors would need the draft to mandate deterministic ML-DSA
signing. See D15 in `pq_edhoc_section3.md`.

## Common parameters

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| SUITES_I | 60 (provisional; see D6) |
| Ephemeral KEM | ML-KEM-512 |
| Static KEM | ML-KEM-512 |
| Signature | ML-DSA-44 |
| Hash | SHA-256 (the draft's suites select SHAKE256; both are 32-byte) |
| AEAD | AES-CCM-16-128-128, 16-byte tag, on any message with a KEM prefix |
| Credentials | by reference (`ID_CRED` = `kid`) |
| EAD | absent in all messages |
